subject: POC evaluation — success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: POC evaluation — success criteria & next steps

Hi Samantha,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through the Acme search assistant use case. As promised, here's a concise recap of the POC goals and a proposed set of success criteria so we can align before we kick off.

Summary of goals
- Validate model/serving stack on Acme customer queries for relevance and latency under realistic traffic
- Measure unit economics (cost/token) and identify straightforward optimizations (caching/quantization)
- Prove rollout path with security controls and auditability for your compliance team

Proposed POC timeline (4 weeks)
- Week 0 (prep, 1 week): access + integration, baseline data ingestion, security checklist
- Week 1 (baseline): run baseline traffic, capture metrics, run initial quality evals
- Week 2 (iter & optimize): apply batching, KV caching, quantization experiments; remeasure
- Week 3 (final eval & handoff): run final automated + human evals, handoff docs, next steps/contract

Ownership
- Redwood technical lead: Jordan Blake (me) — integration, eval harness, model selection
- Redwood infra/ops: Markus Klein — provisioning, routing, performance SLOs
- Redwood CS: Marissa Cole — success criteria, scheduling, customer ops
- Security & compliance contact: Dev Patel (for KMS/audit log coordination)

Success criteria / KPIs (proposed, please iterate)
- Latency: p95 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 300 ms (95th/99th tail under real traffic)
- Throughput: sustain 150 concurrent requests (avg response ~100 tokens) with <= 5% error rate
- Cost: gross cost/token <= $0.0005 (target; we’ll show delta with batching/quant)
- Quality: automated eval F1 >= 0.82 (task-specific), human rating >= 4.0/5 on 100-sample set
- Reliability: <1% request failure and full traceability of requests (audit logs)

Required inputs from Acme
- Dev access: test API key or temporary ingest point for representative queries
- Sample evaluation set + business rules for correctness
- Security contact to complete quick SOC/Sec questionnaire (we'll provide)

Attachments: POC-success-criteria-v1.docx (outline), poc-eval-plan.xlsx (evaluation checklist)

Next steps
- If this looks good, propose we target May 17 for a 60–90 minute kickoff (integration + access)
- I'll put together a deeper evaluation plan and a HubSpot record with milestones once you confirm

Appreciate the partnership — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to iterate on the KPIs.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Thanks — got the security doc, appreciated. Quick answers and an updated, slightly more detailed plan below.

Security/retention notes
- We can provide a PII-safe ingest pattern and retain logs for the POC window only (configurable; default 30 days).
- We’ll send the SOC2 summary + a short answers doc for your security lead by EOD tomorrow. Dev will coordinate KMS/IAM details.

Procurement note
- Typical path: POC -> short-term pilot contract (1–3 months) -> committed Dedicated/Annual contract. I’ll draft a 1-page procurement summary and attach it to the HubSpot deal.

Updated KPIs & eval plan (high level)
- Latency: p95 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 300 ms; measure under simulated traffic matching your peak query mix
- Throughput: sustain >= 150 RPS with average response sizes (~100 tokens); target <5% error rate
- Cost: target gross cost <= $0.0005 / token (we’ll show before/after of batching + quantization)
- Quality: automated eval: F1 >= 0.82 on your labeled set; human eval: >= 4.0/5 on a 100-sample blind set
- Operational: collection of request traces, per-request latency/cost breakdowns, and audit logs available to your security team

Proposed immediate next steps
- Confirm kickoff: May 17, 10:00 PT (60–90m) — onboarding + access exchange
- Deliverables before kickoff: Redwood sends SOC2 summary + short answers; Acme provides sample eval set + a temporary API key or ingest endpoint
- Week-by-week milestones added to HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/ACME-67890

I’ve uploaded a working evaluation checklist to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPOC-Acme — will update as we go.

If that schedule looks good I’ll calendar the kickoff and include a short agenda.

Best,
Jordan
